story:
A mortal Trojan prince, cousin to the Trojan king, fathered a son by the goddess of love. The king of the gods had made the goddess desire the prince; she appeared to him disguised as a mortal princess, seduced him, then revealed her true identity, warning him never to tell anyone he had lain with a goddess. She bore a son, gave him to mountain nymphs to raise until age five, then delivered him to his father. The father later boasted of the affair and was struck lame in one foot by a thunderbolt from the king of the gods, so that in later years his son had to carry him.

In the war against the Greeks, the son was an honorable warrior, twice saved from death by the gods. He led an attack to recover the body of his brother-in-law and commanded allied troops as cousin to the chief Trojan warrior. His mother and a god of prophecy rescued him from a duel with a Greek hero and healed him; the sea god also saved him from another great hero, declaring he was destined to become king of his people. He was said to be the one household spared destruction for his piety.

When the city fell, the gods commanded him to flee. He gathered companions, carried the city's sacred household images, and bore his lame father from the flames. His father died during their travels. A storm drove them to a foreign city, where its queen fell in love with him and proposed joint rule; but a divine messenger reminded him of his destiny, and he departed secretly. The grieving queen cursed his descendants and killed herself upon a pyre.

After another storm, the group held funeral games for the dead father in an island, then reached Italy, where the son descended to the underworld, met the dead queen (who turned away from him) and his father, who showed him the future of his descendants. A local king welcomed the exiles, and despite his daughter's betrothal to a rival king, a prophecy destined her to marry the newcomer instead. War followed, aided by hostile gods and allied kings, but the newcomer prevailed and killed the rival. He founded a city named for his wife, welcomed his lost queen's sister, who later killed herself from jealousy, and after his own death was made a god: a river god cleansed his mortal parts and his mother anointed him with divine substances. He became ancestor of the twin founders of a great city, raised in infancy by a she-wolf.
